en: The Ekākṣara Upaniṣad I worship Nārāyaṇa, who is established in the single-syllabled word, who is the self of all, indivisible, pure consciousness devoid of all else, and who consists of three parts. Oṃ. May He protect us both; may He nourish us both; may we work together with great vigor; may our study be full of splendor; may we never harbor enmity toward one another. Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.
Hari, Oṃ!
That single syllable exists here within the Imperishable, in Soma, and here in the Suṣumṇā; it is that one who is firm.
You are the source of the universe, the Lord of beings, the Ancient One; you alone are Parjanya, the protector of the world. (1)
O Jātavedas, you are the Lord of the universe, whose path all poets have lost;
he who was unborn in the beginning, that very one of golden seed, the ancient and sole sovereign, is you alone through sacrifices. (2)
Prāṇa, the source of procreation and the womb of the world, the entire universe is pervaded by you with a single step.
You are the source of all beings, the shore beyond the womb; within your own embryo, you are the one youth, the arrow-less one, the wielder of the excellent bow.
Spreading your arrow, which has the color of the rising sun, you shine in the midst of the sky like Hiraṇyagarbha;
by your radiance, Tārkṣya was created in the firmament—you are indeed Kumāra, you are Ariṣṭanemi.
You are the wielder of the thunderbolt, the Lord of Beings; you alone are Kāma, deposited within the *soma* of all creatures.
You are *svāhā*, *svadhā*, and that which one utters as *vaṣaṭ*; you are Rudra, submerged in the secret cave of the senses. (5)
You are the Ordainer, the Disposer, the Purifier, the Winged One, Viṣṇu, the Boar, Night, and Solitude;
you are the past, the future, the Source, and ritual actions; you are Time, Sequence, and the Supreme Imperishable.

From Your mouth issue forth the Ṛg-veda verses, the Yajus formulas, and the Sāman chants; O Sovereign, You are the Vasu, the intermediate space, the leader of sacrifice, the consumer of oblations, the all-pervading one, as well as the Rudras, the hosts of Daityas, and the Vasus.
This very god, moving through the sky, presides over other wheels and restrains darkness;
he whose golden form shines as everything within the expanse of space, like the hub with its rays.
He is the knower of all, the protector of the world; by those [powers] he is established among the people of all creatures.
You are the warp and the woof, the discernment of the steps; you are Prajāpati, composed of meters, free from the womb.
You alone are he whose ends are the Sāman chants, whose arms are pure and golden, and who is the most excellent among those who know the Vedas;
you are the one whom the knowers of Brahman praise at the sacrifice with Sāmans, Yajus, and ritual acts. 10.
You are woman, you are man, and you alone are the youth; you indeed are the maiden, and you alone are the earth.
You alone are the Creator (Dhātṛ), Varuṇa the king, the year, Agni, and Aryaman—you are everything.
You are Mitra, Suparṇa, Candra, Indra, Rudra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Viṣṇu, Savitṛ, and the Lord of Cattle;
you are Viṣṇu, and you protect all beings from the Daityas; the world, containing the source of creation within its womb, is pervaded by you.
You are Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ; for you are indeed the Self-born One, facing every direction.
He who thus eternally knows the Lord, dwelling in the cave of the heart, the ancient one, present in all beings, and golden-hued—[he attains liberation].
The golden one, the supreme goal of the wise—he, being wise, stands having transcended wisdom; such is the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ! May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together;
may we work together with great vigor;
may our study be powerful; may we never harbor mutual hatred.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the Ekākṣara Upaniṣad.
